title: 2. What the Company Does: Segments, Revenue Mix & Concrete Examples
book_title: Chapter 2: Inside Every Segment — Products, Customers & Real-World Examples

epigraph.quote: We do not sell what sells; we sell what we ourselves buy, backed by math and simplicity.
epigraph.author: Feroze Azeez, Joint CEO, Anand Rathi Wealth Ltd

web_blocks.html: Anand Rathi Wealth reports a single statutory segment: 'Sale and distribution of financial products.' Operationally, the business runs three distinct verticals [2][3][13]. (1) Private Wealth (PW) generates roughly 96%–97% of consolidated revenue. (2) Digital Wealth (DW) is a B2C phygital platform for mass-affluent investors. (3) Omni Financial Advisors (OFA) is a B2B2C SaaS platform for independent Mutual Fund Distributors (MFDs). Together, DW and OFA contribute ~3%–4% of revenue and act as long-term client and distributor incubation funnels [3][13].

web_blocks.takeaway: Private Wealth remains the economic engine (~96%–97% of revenue), with Mutual Fund distribution alone growing 22% YoY to Rs 494 Cr in FY26 alongside a steady 28% AUM allocation to Structured Products.

web_blocks.html: 1. Private Wealth — Equity Mutual Funds (51% of FY26 AUM, Rs 494 Cr MF Revenue): Consider a Pune auto-ancillary promoter who sells a minority stake for Rs 25 crore. She wants liquid, inflation-beating wealth compounding without managing 40 individual stocks. The ARWL Relationship Manager runs a quantitative diagnostic and allocates Rs 15–16 crore (~65% of the core portfolio) into 6–8 diversified open-ended equity mutual funds [3]. The basket spans large-cap, flexi-cap, and mid-cap funds. ARWL charges zero upfront load. Instead, asset managers pay ARWL an annual trail commission (typically 70–90 bps) for as long as the family stays invested [3][8].

2. Private Wealth — Structured Products / Non-PPMLDs (28% of FY26 AUM): The remaining Rs 7–8 crore of that promoter's portfolio is earmarked for stability rather than pure equity volatility. Here, ARWL recommends Non-Principal Protected Market Linked Debentures (Non-PPMLDs) with a 3-to-5-year tenor. These are predominantly issued by group NBFC Anand Rathi Global Finance Ltd (ARGFL) or select third-party issuers [15][19]. In a typical payoff, if the Nifty 50 finishes flat or down up to 25%–30% at maturity, the investor earns a predefined coupon (e.g., 10%–12% annualized) [19]. Principal is at risk only if the Nifty breaches a deep knock-in barrier at maturity. ARWL earns a placement spread from the issuer, while post-Finance Act 2023 rules tax all MLD gains at the investor's slab rate [18].

3. Digital Wealth (DW) & Omni Financial Advisors (OFA): Consider a Bengaluru software architect with Rs 75 lakh of investable surplus, below Private Wealth's Rs 5 crore+ threshold. She onboards via ARWL's mobile app paired with a remote advisor, receiving automated rebalancing and goal tracking. By FY26, Digital Wealth reached Rs 2,218 crore in AUM across 7,106 clients [13]. Meanwhile, in OFA, a Jaipur independent Mutual Fund Distributor managing Rs 25 crore across 180 families pays an annual SaaS subscription. She gets OFA's white-labeled CRM, portfolio reporting, and transaction engine. By FY26, 6,906 MFDs managed ~Rs 1.5 lakh crore of client assets on OFA [13].

web_blocks.title: The Dual-Engine Reality: Trail Annuity vs. Structured Product Margin
paragraphs: Mutual Fund distribution revenue rose 52% in FY25 (to Rs 406 Cr) and 22% in FY26 (to Rs 494 Cr), providing high-visibility recurring trail income [7][8].

However, MF revenue still represents ~41% of FY26 adjusted total revenue (Rs 494 Cr on Rs 1,198.5 Cr) [8]. The larger share of revenue and profitability still comes from structured product distribution—where margins per rupee of AUM are materially higher than mutual fund trail fees, creating both superior ROE and higher regulatory/issuer sensitivity.

book_paragraphs: If you want to understand why Anand Rathi Wealth earns nearly 47% operating margins while most wealth managers struggle at 25% to 30%, you have to look past the statutory filing—which lumps everything into one line called 'Sale and distribution of financial products'—and examine the three distinct engines humming underneath.

The first engine is Private Wealth Mutual Fund Distribution, which brought in Rs 494 crore of revenue in FY26, up 22% year-on-year. Picture a business owner in Surat who just sold a factory plot for Rs 20 crore. They are terrified of timing the market, yet terrified of inflation eating their fixed deposits. An Anand Rathi RM sits down with them, maps out their liquidity needs, and places roughly Rs 13 crore into a disciplined basket of diversified equity mutual funds. Notice how the cash register rings: Anand Rathi does not charge a fat upfront check. Instead, it collects a quiet, recurring trail fee—roughly 0.7% to 0.9% a year—for every year that family stays invested. In Q2 FY27 alone, clients poured a record Rs 2,867 crore of net inflows into equity mutual funds.

Now look at the second engine inside Private Wealth: Structured Products, specifically Non-PPMLDs, which represent 28% of total AUM. Why do wealthy Indian families put nearly three out of every ten rupees here? Because human psychology hates losing money twice as much as it loves making it. Suppose that same Surat entrepreneur wants Rs 5 crore to earn equity-like returns without the stomach-churning risk of a 20% market drop. The RM offers a 3-to-5-year Market Linked Debenture linked to the Nifty 50: as long as the Nifty does not crash below a deep barrier—say 30% down—at maturity, the client walks away with a pre-agreed coupon. The catch? That debenture is a debt obligation of the issuer—frequently Anand Rathi Global Finance—and since the Finance Act 2023, its gains are taxed at peak income-tax slab rates rather than the old 10% LTCG rate. Yet demand has stayed sticky because the pre-tax risk-adjusted payoff still appeals to conservative HNIs.

Finally, you and I should not overlook the two small incubation labs: Digital Wealth and Omni Financial Advisors. Together they are just 3% to 4% of revenue today, but they solve a clever strategic problem. Digital Wealth serves 7,106 mass-affluent clients (Rs 10 lakh to Rs 5 crore) who are too small for a dedicated Private Wealth RM today—yet some of them will sell a business or inherit wealth tomorrow. And OFA is a pure SaaS toolkit used by 6,906 independent mutual fund distributors managing Rs 1.5 lakh crore of assets. It turns potential competitors into paying software subscribers. That is how a focused firm covers the entire wealth pyramid without bloating its headcount.

book_callouts.title: Narrator's Reflection: Why 41% MF Revenue Matters
paragraphs: When you divide Rs 494 crore of mutual fund revenue by Rs 1,198.5 crore of FY26 adjusted total revenue, you get 41.2%. That means nearly 59% of the top line comes from structured products and other financial distribution.

This mix is a double-edged sword: it is the reason ARWL's revenue yield on AUM (~1.3% blended) is much higher than pure MF distributors, and it is also the exact reason we must scrutinize issuer credit risk and tax policy in Chapters 4 and 6.
